name: react-native-spritestudio
description: SpriteStudio animation player for React Native (New Architecture / Nitro + Skia)
//peerDependencies: One line, and it is the line the root `overrides` pin: whatever Expo's
compatibility table chose for example/. Everything that has ever built or
run here -- typecheck, the unit tests, the example app, the host checks --
ran against that line, so a wider range would claim a version nobody has
compiled the Nitro/Skia side against. Move these with the overrides when
the example's Expo SDK moves, not when the registry does; that is also why
Dependabot is told to leave these five alone.
The caret does the right thing on both shapes: ^0.86.2 is the 0.86 line
(npm locks the minor below 1.0.0), ^2.11.0 and ^4.5.3 span their majors.
//devDependencies: `react-test-renderer` is pinned to the exact `react` the root `overrides`
chose, not a caret: React refuses to run against a renderer from a
different build, so the two move together. It is deprecated in React 19 and
is still the only renderer that does not need a DOM, which is what the
`view/` tests need -- @testing-library/react-native sits on it for the same
reason. Move it when react moves.
//publishConfig: npm tags whatever is published as `latest` regardless of the prerelease identifier, so a 7.0.0-beta.1 with no tag here would be what a bare `npm i react-native-spritestudio` installs. `beta` matches the identifier in the version and what SSPlayerForWgpu publishes under.
//browser: Not web support — the stub barrel, so an app that ships web as well as native can still build its web bundle (src/index.web.ts). Still points at source while `main` resolves into lib/; moving it there is the open half of the npm-publishing item in ROADMAP.md.
